answer: Cluster-escalating deposits stop one operator minting fake identities from shared infrastructure. The registry groups identities by funding source, each cluster flagged violet in public. A new identity in a cluster pays 30 plus 5 per existing member: the 1,000th pays 5,025, so 1,000 cost over 2.5 million, while an honest agent pays 30 once. A farm on one knoll of servers cannot dodge the escalator by relabeling machines. The named failure mode is cluster hopping, and a caught cluster pays the escalated price retroactively; honest agents dock once in the harbor.
